articles.title: NFL Refs to Work Back-to-Back Games After FAA Stoppage Impacts Travel Schedules
articles.summary: It is reportedly going to be a busy Sunday for a handful of NFL officials.
articles.body:
It is reportedly going to be a busy Sunday for a handful of NFL officials.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported referee Don Willard, umpire Terry Killens, field judge Jabir Walker and side judge Justin Larrew will all work Sunday's game between the Miami Dolphins and Indianapolis Colts in Indianapolis at 1 p.m. ET before traveling to Cincinnati to also work the night game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals at 8:20 p.m. ET.

They are doing so because the NFL adjusted officiating assignments in an effort to "avoid further travel issues," per Schefter, after the Federal Aviation Administration grounded nationwide flights for hours on Friday.

Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said the stoppage happened because of "a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers."

While the NFL had to adjust the officiating schedule, it didn't face as many challenges as college football since many teams travel the day before their game on Fridays.

ESPN noted a number of kickoff times were changed because of travel issues. Most notably, the game between Ole Miss and Oklahoma was moved from Saturday to Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

Elsewhere, a number of NBA and NHL teams faced travel issues.

It reached a point that Colorado State even held a walk-through at the airport:

Duffy said in a Friday press conference that college football teams that were facing challenges should contact the FAA directly:

According to Google Maps , the driving time between Indianapolis and Cincinnati is approximately one hour and 45 minutes without significant game traffic. If the game between the Colts and Dolphins ends around 4:15 p.m. ET, the officials will likely have enough time to make it to Cincinnati with some time to warm up before the Bengals and Steelers kick off.

Still, it is a quick turnaround that could be impacted by traffic.

Schefter reported the officiating schedule was changed by "reassigning officials to games within driving distance of their hometown."

As for the game itself, it is a massively important one in the AFC North. Cincinnati and Pittsburgh are tied for first place in the division at 6-2, and the winner will be right in the middle of the race for the AFC's No. 1 seed as well.

articles.title: Kirk Cousins to Make NFL History with Ultra Rare Stat After Trade to Vikings from Raiders
articles.summary: Kirk Cousins is about to make NFL history.
articles.body:
Kirk Cousins is about to make NFL history.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the veteran will become the first quarterback to start back-to-back weeks for different teams since the starting stat was officially measured beginning in 1950 when he takes the field for the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday.

Cousins started the Las Vegas Raiders' game against the San Francisco 49ers last Sunday before the AFC West team traded him to Minnesota.

What's more, Schefter noted Cousins will also become the first signal-caller in NFL history to start a playoff game for one team after starting for another during that season if the Vikings do reach the postseason.

Whether Minnesota does reach the playoffs will likely depend largely on Cousins' play.

After all, they have a dominant defense that is first in the league in points allowed per game and second in yards allowed per game. That unit is a primary reason the team is 6-2 and in the middle of the playoff picture.

Yet quarterback play has been a concern.

Kyler Murray had just five touchdown passes to three interceptions in six games before he was sidelined by a hamstring injury. NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Saturday that Murray is still "a couple of weeks away" from returning.

Carson Wentz played in his spot during the team's matchup with the Buffalo Bills and went 8-for-25 passing for 81 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions. That game happened right before the NFL's trade deadline, which underscored the need to do something at the position so the defense didn't go to waste.

The four-time Pro Bowler previously played for the Vikings from 2018 through 2023, so he is familiar with head coach Kevin O'Connell's system and has chemistry with go-to receiver Justin Jefferson.

It should be a fairly smooth transition for him after arriving from the Raiders, which will allow him to make history Sunday when the Vikings put him right into the starting lineup for a key divisional game against the Packers.

articles.title: Drake Maye Injured, Latest Updates on Patriots QB After Ankle Injury vs. Lions

articles.body:
The New England Patriots announced quarterback Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury and was ruled out against the Detroit Lions on Sunday.

Maye was seen going to the locker room with an apparent limp during the first quarter:

Maye has started all 10 games for the Patriots this season after starting all 17 during the team's 2025 campaign. He also started all four playoff games during the team's run to the last Super Bowl.

The No. 3 overall pick of the 2024 NFL draft has been fairly durable throughout the early portion of his career, which is one reason he reached the Pro Bowl in each of his first two seasons.

However, this setback meant New England had to turn toward Tommy DeVito under center against a formidable Lions team that entered play with a 6-2 record.

Maye has had something of an up-and-down 2026 season, as he completed 65.4 percent of his passes for 2,282 yards and 18 touchdowns in his first nine games. Yet he also entered Sunday's matchup leading the NFL with 11 interceptions.

Three of those picks came in the last game against the Green Bay Packers, so he was surely looking to bounce back Sunday against the Lions.

The timing of the injury is particularly concerning for New England, as it dropped two of its last three games to fall to 5-4 on the season. It is tied with the Cleveland Browns in the race for the AFC's final wild-card spot and doesn't have much room for error in the standings department.

A prolonged absence for Maye would put the reigning AFC champion's playoff chances in serious doubt.

articles.title: Aidan Hutchinson Injured Celebrating, Latest on Lions Star After Exiting vs. Patriots

articles.body:
The Detroit Lions ruled out Aidan Hutchinson from Sunday's game against the New England Patriots with a knee injury.

Hutchinson was hurt when he landed awkwardly after celebrating a sack on New England's opening drive of the first quarter.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport described Hutchinson as doing a "full Gramatica." Former Arizona Cardinals kicker Bill Gramatica tore his ACL while celebrating a made field goal in a 2001 game.

Hutchinson enjoyed a return to form in 2025 after fractures to his tibia and fibula limited him to five games a season earlier. He had 14.5 sacks en route to earning a second Pro Bowl nod and finishing fifth in the Defensive Player of the Year voting.

The fifth-year pass-rusher was delivering more of the same through the Lions' first eight games. He had five sacks and 18 hits on the quarterback, and he made his presence felt early Sunday by bringing down Patriots quarterback Drake Maye.

Entering Week 10, Detroit was allowing 355 yards per game, which is tied for 26th, and ranks last in pass defense (260.9). That's despite totaling the third-most sacks (27) in the NFL.

Losing Hutchinson for any period of time would be a massive blow for the unit.

articles.title: Baker Mayfield Injured, Latest NFL Rumors on Bucs QB's Status and Recovery Timeline
articles.summary: When the Tampa Bay Buccaneers return to action in Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season, they may be without their starting quarterback.
articles.body:
When the Tampa Bay Buccaneers return to action in Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season, they may be without their starting quarterback.

NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported Mayfield suffered an injury to his lower leg in the 27-24 loss to the Chicago Bears. He "has been in and out of a walking boot in recent days as a way of rehabbing and resting the injury."

Garafolo noted the Buccaneers haven't made any decisions as to his availability against the Detroit Lions: "No one has ruled Mayfield out of next week's game in Detroit, and several sources have noted his willingness to play through injuries in the past. If it's a question of pain tolerance over functionality, according to sources, Mayfield will do everything he can to take the field against the Lions."

A dislocated right thumb sidelined Mayfield for three games, and he registered little impact upon returning in Week 7. Between the wins over the Carolina Panthers and Atlanta Falcons, he threw a total of 14 passes.

The two-time Pro Bowler looked more like his usual self against Chicago, only to suffer a new injury.

Tampa Bay has already gotten to experience life with Jalon Daniels as QB1. He had 501 passing yards, three touchdowns and four interceptions in his three starts.

In general, Daniels performed as you'd expect from an undrafted rookie. He had moments when his inexperience showed.

The Bucs haven't added to their quarterback room since Mayfield was reactivated. Daniels remains the only other QB on the roster, so he'd be in line to step up against Detroit if circumstances require it.

Once again, the overall state of the NFC South is helping Tampa Bay maintain playoff aspirations despite owning a losing record (3-6). That's only a half-game worse than the Carolina Panthers and New Orleans Saints.

Still, any loss could be costly for the Buccaneers at this point. They'll hope having extra time off will allow for Mayfield to suit up in Week 11.

articles.title: Lions star Aidan Hutchinson injures knee while celebrating sack of Drake Maye
articles.summary: Aidan Hutchinson leapt into the air after a sack and came down hard.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson made his presence known early against the New England Patriots. On the Patriots' first offensive drive, Hutchinson broke through the line on third down and sacked Drake Maye.

Following the play, Hutchinson got up to celebrate the sack. He jumped into the air and immediately fell to the ground after landing. Hutchinson appeared to be holding his right knee.

Hutchinson was able to walk off the field, but headed straight to the medical tent on the sideline. He was later spotted on the broadcast heading to the locker room.

He was deemed questionable to return with a knee injury, but late in the third quarter, he was ruled out for the remainder of the game.

Hutchinson wasn't the only player injured on the play. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye also left the game . He was deemed questionable to return due to an ankle injury.

Even before that play, Hutchinson already made a big impact in the game. On the play before his injury, he smartly rushed across the line of scrimmage once he noticed the play clock ran out. His quick thinking resulted in the Patriots being charged with a delay of game, setting up a third and long.

Losing Hutchinson for any significant period of time would be a devastating result for the Lions. Coming into the game, Hutchinson was Pro Football Focus' top-graded edge rusher on the year.

While NFL players rarely get injured while celebrating plays, it has happened before. Back in 2001, Arizona Cardinals kicker Bill Gramatica tore his ACL after celebrating a first quarter field goal in a game against the New York Giants.

articles.title: 'I want to beat them absolutely.' Dallas Cowboys to face 49ers
articles.summary: Dallas hasn't beaten the San Francisco 49ers since 2020. Cowboys look to end the streak.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are hoping to light a spark when they face the San Francisco 49ers in one of the NFL's most-storied rivalries.

The Cowboys (4-5) take on the 49ers (7-1) in a Week 10 game at 2:25 p.m. MT/ 3:25 p.m. CT on Sunday, Nov. 15, at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. The game will air on FOX.

San Francisco has won four straight against Dallas, including two playoff games. The last Cowboys win over the 49ers was in 2020 at home with limited attendance due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

The Cowboys have yet to beat a team with a winning record this season. Dallas earned a 27-23 victory over the Indianapolis Colts (2-7) last week.

Last week, the 49ers bounced back from their first loss of the season with a 38-17 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders .

"I want to beat them absolutely," Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott told DallasCowboys.com . "And I'm not naive to what has happened or my history against them. But to put that on the rest of these guys or put that on the locker room, I think that's stupid. This is about us going in and getting a win. And us trying to win this game and get some momentum going and get back-to-back wins for the first time this season and build off of that."

"So, what a great opportunity to get to do it against a 7-1 team. It just so happens that it be the Niners," Prescott said.

"Obviously I want to get a win and everybody in this building does for a bunch of different reasons. But at the end of the day, it's a 7-1 team coming in here and we've got an opportunity to beat them. We've got to go do everything we can to get that done."

Dallas Cowboys vs. San Francisco 49ers series record

The Cowboys are in the NFC East and the 49ers are in the NFC West, so both teams do not play each other regularly.

The rivalry was forged in the postseason, particularly in the 1970s, '80s and '90s. The teams have faced each other in the playoffs nine times.

The 49ers lead the overall series, 21–19–1. But the Cowboys hold a 5-4 record in the playoffs.

The only tie took place on a 24-24 Thanksgiving Day game played in the Cotton Bowl in Dallas in 1969.

The Dallas Cowboys play the 49ers at 2:25 p.m. MT/ 3:25 p.m. CT on Nov. 15 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. The game will air on FOX.
